Learn Hub/KYC & Urgency Traps

Bank KYC Expiry, Electricity Cutoff & SIM Deactivation Threats

Published: October 2026·RBI & TRAI Consumer Advisory·Estimated Reading Time: 4 mins
The Daily Attack

Unlike grand digital arrest operations, “Utility Urgency” scams hit millions of Indian mobile subscribers daily. Attackers send spoofed SMS messages warning of power cutoff at 9:30 PM, bank account suspension within 24 hours, or SIM card disconnection due to non-updated Aadhaar biometric records.

The Three Common Variants

1. The Electricity / Power Disconnection Threat

“Dear consumer, your electricity will be disconnected tonight at 9:30 PM from the power office because your previous month's bill was not updated. Please immediately contact our electricity officer at 98xxxxxx.”

When the elder calls, they are told to pay a token ₹10 fee via a malicious link or install an app like AnyDesk or RustDesk so the “officer” can fix the error. The app then captures their bank MPIN and drains accounts.

2. Bank Account KYC Suspension

“SBI/HDFC Alert: Your NetBanking account will be blocked today due to pending re-KYC. Click here to verify your PAN card and Aadhaar details.”

The link loads a near-identical phishing portal mimicking State Bank of India or HDFC. The elder enters their user ID, password, and OTP, granting instant access to attackers.

3. TRAI Mobile Number Disconnection

An automated voice claims: “This call is from the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI). Your mobile number will be terminated within 2 hours due to illegal advertising and harassment complaints.”

TRAI has officially clarified that it NEVER calls individual telecom subscribers to disconnect phone numbers.

RBI Golden Rules for Elders

  • Never download screen-sharing APKs: No legitimate bank or utility electricity board will ever ask you to install AnyDesk, TeamViewer, or QuickSupport on your mobile phone.
  • OTP is strictly private: Bank staff and electricity officers never require OTP or debit card CVV numbers to verify accounts.
  • Always pay bills through official utility apps: Use official state electricity portals (e.g. BESCOM, MSEDCL, TPDDL) or established UPI apps rather than numbers sent in SMS.
Emergency Action Advisory
Hang up immediately and call 1930 or visit cybercrime.gov.in

If you shared an OTP or downloaded a screen-sharing tool, switch on Airplane Mode immediately and call 1930 to freeze unauthorized debit transfers.
